MC	<p>926e_30b9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #23648b;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #23648b;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #23648b;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9a2f67;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, emy, +++, emy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d161_05b6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d02;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #884d02;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d02;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #23648b;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #23648b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #23648b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873a89;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #873a89;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #873a89;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fnt, +++, fnt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4f6f_fd5b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873a89;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #873a89;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #873a89;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mtx, +++, mtx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c27d_823b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #77580c;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #77580c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #77580c;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dey, +++, dey"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b0fc_dbad</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d02;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #884d02;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d02;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #236e3a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #365d9d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, epx, +++, epx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6492_e558</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9d343d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bdn, +++, bdn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6fe4_48ab</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d02;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #884d02;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d02;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e58;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e58;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e58;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7143a4;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, efk, +++, efk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0ab7_fa97</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #77580c;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #77580c;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #77580c;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #23648b;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #23648b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #23648b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9a2f67;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ach, +++, ach"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>dd30_9d24</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #77580c;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #77580c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #77580c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #23648b;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #23648b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #23648b;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9a2f67;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ekr, +++, ekr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9c51_f3d1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9a2f67;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bem, +++, bem"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bbd6_0d0b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9d343d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #365d9d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bnp, +++, bnp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7951_381b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfr, +++, cfr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>55f3_4cbc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>7c5c_b611</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d02;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #884d02;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d02;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #236e3a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #23648b;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #23648b;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #23648b;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kmr, +++, kmr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f607_208d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9d343d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, chn, +++, chn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f7b0_a7b1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #236e3a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7143a4;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>ab8c_3a21</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7143a4;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dhy, +++, dhy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bc1c_751b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9d343d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cef, +++, cef"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>cdcd_a50a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9d343d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e58;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e58;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e58;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #365d9d;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>4e05_bffd</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d02;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #884d02;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d02;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #236e3a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fmt, +++, fmt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3ba5_7ce4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #23648b;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #23648b;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #23648b;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9a2f67;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, emx, +++, emx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>044e_d916</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d02;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #884d02;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d02;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #23648b;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #23648b;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #23648b;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873a89;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #873a89;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>fb48_53f6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cdr, +++, cdr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b418_1ae9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9d343d;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dfh, +++, dfh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>64b5_94d0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697e;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00697e;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697e;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, rwx, +++, rwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d3e8_0612</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #236e3a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #365d9d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ejm, +++, ejm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4410_39ab</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #77580c;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #77580c;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #77580c;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873a89;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #873a89;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #873a89;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abk, +++, abk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>e7e7_478a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d02;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #884d02;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d02;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e58;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e58;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e58;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #365d9d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>398c_f611</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7143a4;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfx, +++, cfx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0a6c_837b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #77580c;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #77580c;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #77580c;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873a89;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #873a89;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #873a89;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jtw, +++, jtw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>26ff_b5e4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, akt, +++, akt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>76b1_477d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #23648b;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #23648b;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #23648b;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873a89;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #873a89;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #873a89;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, adm, +++, adm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d1c3_0c35</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ajr, +++, ajr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9604_0bde</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d02;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #884d02;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d02;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ahm, +++, ahm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4ddb_8717</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bkx, +++, bkx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
