MC	<p>1760_1d2b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e58;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e58;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e58;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #514fb4;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #514fb4;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, htx, +++, htx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5d85_7a0f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9d343d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #236e3a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #23648b;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #23648b;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #23648b;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kty, +++, kty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3128_fe91</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7143a4;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, chp, +++, chp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5b49_4f5b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d02;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #884d02;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d02;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #236e3a;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7143a4;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jry, +++, jry"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>88ca_468b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697e;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7143a4;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hky, +++, hky"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c326_db75</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697e;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #00697e;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697e;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7143a4;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ben, +++, ben"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3e8a_4459</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d02;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #884d02;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d02;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e58;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e58;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e58;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #365d9d;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cer, +++, cer"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>44a5_00ab</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9d343d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697e;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00697e;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697e;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kwx, +++, kwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0300_2116</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d02;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #884d02;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d02;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7143a4;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ekr, +++, ekr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ae55_9c43</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9d343d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #23648b;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #23648b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #23648b;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, knx, +++, knx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ed4b_ab8f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #236e3a;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #365d9d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #365d9d;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9a2f67;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, rty, +++, rty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>fc8c_4d69</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9a3d12;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3d12;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697e;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00697e;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697e;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7143a4;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ajk, +++, ajk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>780c_0329</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #236e3a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236e3a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #23648b;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #23648b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #23648b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9a2f67;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2f67;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hnw, +++, hnw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697e;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00697e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7143a4;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7143a4;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, akp, +++, akp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>936c_58b8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9d343d;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d343d;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #496a13;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #496a13;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496a13;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697e;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697e;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697e;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, rwx, +++, rwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
